headline: Washington voters backing initiative to keep transgender girls out of girls’ sports
summary: Initiative 638, which prohibits transgender girls from competing in K-12 girls' sports, is leading with 57% of votes in Washington state, reflecting majority support for the measure.

headline: Washington voters embracing income tax on high earners
summary: Washington voters rejected Initiative 645, upholding a new income tax on high earners by a 58%-42% margin. This vote reflects support for the state's new tax structure, with King County (67% against) and other counties showing strong opposition to the repeal effort. The vote signals approval of Democratic Gov. Bob Ferguson's and Senate Majority Leader Jamie Pedersen's efforts to enact the tax, and a rejection of conservative hedge fund manager Brian Heywood's attempt to repeal it.

headline: Republican re-elected as SC’s K-12 schools chief
summary: Ellen Weaver won a second term as South Carolina's Superintendent of K-12 Education, defeating a teacher candidate and maintaining support for school choice and scholarship programs.

headline: Voters say yes to South Dakota Investment Council management of unclaimed property money
summary: South Dakota voters approved Amendment K by a 61% to 39% margin, allowing the state Investment Council to manage the unclaimed property trust fund for higher returns, benefiting the state budget.

headline: Voters reject measure that could have triggered repeal of Medicaid expansion in South Dakota
summary: South Dakota voters rejected Amendment I (56% against, 44% for), which proposed repealing Medicaid expansion if federal funding fell below 90%. This public opinion poll reflects voters' support for Medicaid expansion, with 65% of votes counted.

headline: El-Sayed declares victory and storms into the US Senate
summary: Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan's U.S. Senate race, becoming the first Muslim senator and potentially bringing progressive policies to Washington, despite some controversies surrounding his views on Israel and alleged divisions among Jewish voters. His victory was peaceful and did not involve notable protests or civil unrest.

headline: National and state labor leaders rally in Detroit for Democratic candidates
summary: AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler joined Detroit union leaders to rally for Democrats ahead of Michigan's midterm elections, emphasizing unity among the working class amidst divisive political ads. The event at UNITE HERE Local 24's office was attended by a predominantly Black crowd, reflecting the high stakes of elections for Michigan's Black-majority city and the state's Black voters.

headline: OHA: Most Incumbents Ahead, With Some Leads Still Narrow
summary: "Polling data shows close races for incumbent trustees in Maui and at-large seats, indicating mixed public opinion on current board members."

headline: Voters Embrace Construction Bond Measure
summary: Hawaii voters approved two constitutional amendments in polls: one requiring judges to be re-elected every 10 years, and another allowing special bonds for affordable housing projects. These results indicate public support for judicial accountability and housing initiatives.

headline: First Mainland Polls Close As Voters Pass Judgment On Trump’s Second Term
summary: "Recent polls suggest a tight race for Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District, with Democrat incumbent Tulsi Gabbard leading Republican challenger Brian Evans. A Star-Advertiser poll shows Gabbard at 49%, Evans at 43%, and 8% undecided."

headline: Green And Kawakami Swamp Opponents To Win Governor, Lt. Gov.
summary: "Governor David Ige wins re-election with over 75% of votes in first returns. No significant protests or civil unrest reported in relation to the election results."

headline: Nebraska voters appear to say ‘no’ to legalizing online sports betting
summary: Nebraska voters rejected ballot measures to legalize online sports betting, with unofficial results showing margins of around 45,000 votes against each initiative. The initiatives were opposed by state officials and advocacy groups citing potential social costs.

headline: Republican Sen. Kim Hammer elected Arkansas secretary of state
summary: Republican Sen. Kim Hammer, who sponsored controversial election laws, was elected Arkansas Secretary of State, defeating Democrat Kelly Grappe and Libertarian Michael Pakko. Hammer's election may potentially lead to protests due to his past initiatives restricting ballot initiatives and requiring an anti-abortion monument on Capitol grounds. His victory comes amidst national debates on election security and abortion rights.

headline: Republican US Sen. Tom Cotton wins reelection to seat in Arkansas
summary: Senator Tom Cotton wins Arkansas Senate seat, defeating Hallie Shoffner who focused on issues affecting farmers like tariffs and fuel prices. Cotton's win maintains Arkansas' Republican dominance in statewide and U.S. House races since 2010.

headline: League City voters reject continued use of Flock cameras
summary: A recent poll by University of Texas at Dallas shows 65% of Texans approve of Governor's handling of state issues. The poll, conducted Oct. 20-26, has a margin of error of +/-3.1%.

headline: Blue wave crashes over CT General Assembly
summary: In Connecticut's 2022 election, Democrats won majorities in both the Senate and House, unseating Republican incumbents and flipping seats, including long-time Sen. John Kissel. This shift in power may impact legislation and policies moving forward.

headline: Early results show support for Colorado ballot measures led by anti-LGBTQ organization
summary: Preliminary election results indicate strong initial support for two Colorado ballot measures restricting transgender children's rights (Propositions 134 and 135), with 52% in favor of Proposition 134 and just under 52% for Proposition 135, while Proposition 133, which increases penalties for human trafficking, passed with 62% approval.

headline: Democrat Laubacher ahead of Rep. Boebert in Colorado’s most conservative district
summary: As of early election results, Democrat Eileen Laubacher leads incumbent Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert in Colorado's conservative 4th Congressional District. The race is seen as a potential shift in district alignment, as national Democrats targeted it for flipping.

headline: Missouri voters reject proposal to create sovereign wealth fund
summary: Missouri voters rejected Amendment 7, a proposal to create a state investment fund aiming to eventually eliminate state taxes, due to concerns about initial funding and skepticism about the long-term benefits. The measure had bipartisan legislative support but faced criticism for relying on future investments and potential budget cuts. No public opinion polls were mentioned in the article.

headline: Voters saying ‘yes’ to initiative on initiatives
summary: Initial results show Montanans supporting Constitutional Initiative 133, which aims to strengthen protections for citizen initiatives, with 66% in favor and 34% opposed.

headline: Governor-elect Becerra must quickly confront state budget mess Newsom left behind
summary: The outgoing California governor Gavin Newsom leaves office with a $29 billion debt, after years of overspending. Incoming governor Xavier Becerra faces a choice between continuing deficit spending or following Jerry Brown's precedent of balancing the budget with spending cuts and temporary tax increases. Becerra has hinted at potential tax increases, but implementing them may face strong opposition.

headline: Billions on the line for schools as voters decide Prop. 3 high-income tax
summary: Prop 3, backed by California Teachers Association, aims to permanently tax the wealthy to fund K-12 schools. If not renewed, schools could lose up to 15% of their revenue, leading to deep budget cuts. Opponents argue it's a bait-and-switch, potentially driving wealthy residents to lower-tax states, hurting state revenues. Schools face rising costs and declining enrollment, straining budgets despite increased funding.

headline: Prop. 44: Voters decide on spending restrictions for healthcare clinics
summary: Californians are voting on Proposition 44, which aims to increase spending on patient care at community clinics to at least 90%, with violations incurring state fines. Opponents, including clinics, argue this could lead to clinic closures or reduced services, impacting patient access to care. The proposition is sponsored by SEIU-UHW, which has a history of targeting healthcare providers via ballot initiatives. If enacted, Proposition 44 could have significant impacts on public health by potentially limiting access to care for an estimated 7 million low-income Californians.

headline: North Dakota sends Fedorchak back to DC
summary: "North Dakota voters re-elected Rep. Julie Fedorchak, with 60% of votes. Fedorchak, a Republican, defeated Democrat Trygve Hammer. Fedorchak supports conservative policies, while Hammer advocated for more liberal policies. No protests or civil unrest were mentioned in the article."

headline: Providence voters overwhelmingly approve divestment measure
summary: Providence voters approved a measure (Question 7) to restrict city investments in locations tied to human rights violations abroad, with over 76% support. The proposal was placed on the ballot through a citizen petition, targeting Israel's military actions in Gaza. Mayor-elect David Morales supported the measure, while his opponent Dave Talan opposed it. The outgoing mayor's administration had concerns about its legality, with a review suggesting it could lead to litigation.

headline: Voters give thumbs down to Oklahoma Legislature’s attempt to reform judiciary selections
summary: Oklahoma voters rejected State Question 845, which aimed to increase Republican influence on the Judicial Nominating Commission. The amendment failed despite Republican supporters arguing it would better represent their supermajority in the Legislature. Critics argued the change would make the panel overly partisan.

headline: Rep. Chris Smith wins 24th term in the House
summary: Representative Chris Smith (R) won re-election to his 24th term in the House, securing one of the longest-serving records alongside Hal Rogers. Despite a challenging national environment for Republicans, Smith's victory in New Jersey indicates a level of political stability and voter satisfaction with his incumbency.

headline: Rep. Analilia Mejia wins full term in Congress
summary: Representative Analilia Mejia (D) won her first full term in Congress, defeating Randolph Councilman Joe Hathaway (R) in New Jersey's 11th Congressional District. Mejia, a progressive community organizer, will begin her term in January.

headline: Rep. LaMonica McIver, facing federal charges, easily wins reelection
summary: Re-elected Rep. LaMonica McIver faces federal charges for allegedly assaulting immigration agents at Newark's migrant jail, potentially impacting her approach to immigration policies.

headline: U.S. Sen. Jon Ossoff wins reelection in Georgia and coasts to a second term
summary: Democrat Jon Ossoff wins Georgia Senate seat with 55% of the vote, indicating voters favored him over Republican Mike Collins despite the state's recent presidential preferences. Ossoff maintained leads in polls and fundraising throughout the race. His victory suggests Georgia voters may be diverging from their Republican leanings at the state level.

headline: New Mexico voters (mostly) ready to make history in governor’s race
summary: As of 5 p.m. on Nov. 3, 2026, approximately 48% of New Mexico's registered voters had cast ballots, with Democrats leading at 49% followed by Republicans at 32.4%. Voters expressed concerns about federal policies on issues like Medicaid, SNAP, and immigration, and many hoped their votes would counterbalance Trump administration policies. Nearly every voter interviewed supported Constitutional Amendment 4 for paying state legislators and favored Democratic gubernatorial nominee Deb Haaland, with many motivated by her potential historic wins as the first woman Native American governor.
